Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with diarrhoea for 3 days, abdominal pain, and vomiting.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: • CC: diarrhoea x3 days, abdominal pain, vomiting

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports watery diarrhea for about 3 days.
Patient has frequent urges to pass stool and a near-constant need to be near the toilet.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: frequent urges/near-constant need to be near toilet

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports needing to go to the toilet about every 10 minutes.
Patient describes a sensation of incomplete evacuation with bowel movements.
Patient reports central/peri-umbilical mild abdominal pain.
Abdominal area is slightly tender to palpation by report.
Abdominal pain is sometimes relieved by passing stool or gas.
Patient had one episode of vomiting this morning after eating strawberries.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Vomiting: one episode this morning after eating fruit (strawberries)

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient does not think there was blood in the vomit.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: patient does not think there was blood in vomit

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient believes fluid intake is low and reports not drinking enough water.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Fluid intake: likely low; "not drinking enough water"

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports no clear fever but has had sweating for the last 4 days and is unsure if febrile.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Fever: no clear fever; reported sweating last 4 days but not sure if febrile

Medications.content: Patient uses an inhaler for asthma.
No medications were prescribed during this consult today.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise oral rehydration with plenty of fluids and monitor for signs of dehydration.

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient should monitor for fever and seek GP or urgent review for in-person abdominal exam if temperature develops or symptoms worsen.

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient should stay home until symptoms improve and avoid antibiotics, which are not indicated.

Plan_of_Care.content: If symptoms persist or worsen after 1–2 days, patient should arrange a GP appointment for further assessment and possible investigation given family history.
